command:
set +e
set -uo pipefail
export PATH=/opt/conda/bin:$PATH
export TMPDIR=/tmp HOME=/tmp
cd /tmp

# spawn runs task commands under bash -e; `set -uo pipefail` does not clear it (spawn#707).
#
# Clocking run for the bowtie2 generation + knee sweeps. Deliberately over-provisioned
# (16 vCPU / 64 GiB) so the tool is never what is throttled: the big box is the instrument,
# not the recommendation. The sweep gets sized from what this measures.

echo "== the index must match the pin the build task recorded =="
sha256sum -c bt2index.tar.sha256 || { echo "FAIL: index tar does not match its pin"; exit 1; }
tar -xf bt2index.tar
ls -l GRCh38_fadh*.bt2 | awk '{print "idxfile\t"$9"\t"$5}'

bowtie2 --version | head -1
nproc | awk '{print "nproc\t"$1}'

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- inline instrument
CG=/sys/fs/cgroup
sampler() {
  : > /tmp/samples.tsv
  while : ; do
    mc=$(cat $CG/memory.current 2>/dev/null || echo 0)
    cu=$(awk '/^usage_usec/{print $2; exit}' $CG/cpu.stat 2>/dev/null || echo 0)
    tk=$(df -k /tmp 2>/dev/null | awk 'NR==2{print $3}')
    printf '%s\t%s\t%s\t%s\n' "$(date +%s)" "${mc:-0}" "${cu:-0}" "${tk:-0}" >> /tmp/samples.tsv
    sleep 2
  done
}
sampler & SPID=$!

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- the real workload
# --local, NOT the default end-to-end. This is the match-the-modes rule: bwa soft-clips,
# bowtie2's default does not, and comparing those two gave 82% where --local on the mapped
# set gave 0.9462. The cross-check against bwa-real is the whole reason this index was built
# on bwa's exact reference, so the mode has to match or the comparison measures the mode.
#
# The SAM is never written to disk. 24.1M pairs would be ~15-20 GB of SAM against a tmpfs
# that is half of RAM; instead it streams through awk, which does the counting and emits a
# compact gzipped TSV of high-confidence primary alignments for the bwa comparison.
# awk reads the stream to completion -- never `head` under pipefail, which is SIGPIPE 141.
echo "== bowtie2 --local, whole genome, 24,148,993 read pairs =="
T0=$(date +%s)
bowtie2 --local -p 32 -x GRCh38_fadh \
  -1 SRR062634_1.filt.fastq.gz -2 SRR062634_2.filt.fastq.gz 2> /tmp/bt2align.log \
  | awk 'BEGIN{OFS="\t"}
      /^@/ {next}
      {
        n++; f=$2+0;
        sec=int(f/256)%2; sup=int(f/2048)%2; unm=int(f/4)%2;
        if (sec==0 && sup==0) {
          prim++;
          if (unm==0) { pmap++; if ($5+0>=30) hiq++; }
        }
        if (unm==0) mapped++;
      }
      END{
        print "sam_records\t" n+0;
        print "primary_records\t" prim+0;
        print "primary_mapped\t" pmap+0;
        print "all_mapped_records\t" mapped+0;
        print "primary_mapq30\t" hiq+0;
      }' > /tmp/counts.tsv
BRC=${PIPESTATUS[0]}
T1=$(date +%s)
kill $SPID 2>/dev/null; wait $SPID 2>/dev/null
WALL=$((T1-T0))
echo "bowtie2_rc	$BRC"
echo "bowtie2_wall_s	$WALL"
cat /tmp/counts.tsv
cat /tmp/bt2align.log
test "$BRC" = "0" || { echo "FAIL: bowtie2 exited $BRC"; exit 1; }

awk -F'\t' -v wall="$WALL" '
  NR==1{cu0=$3}
  {if($2>mc)mc=$2; if($4>tk)tk=$4; cu=$3; n++}
  END{
    printf "peak_rss_mib\t%.0f\n", mc/1048576;
    printf "tmpfs_peak_mib\t%.0f\n", tk/1024;
    if(wall>0) printf "avg_cores\t%.2f\n", (cu-cu0)/(wall*1000000);
  }' /tmp/samples.tsv

# ------------------------------------------------- the conservation identity, not a band
# Every read gets exactly one primary record whether it aligns or not, so the primary count
# is fixed by the input: 2 x 24,148,993 pairs = 48,297,986. bwa-real aligned these exact
# bytes, so this is the same denominator both tools must satisfy. A truncated run, a dropped
# mate, or a silently-skipped tile fails this even though the alignment rate would still look
# plausible -- which a band on "% mapped" would not catch.
PRIM=$(awk -F'\t' '$1=="primary_records"{print $2}' /tmp/counts.tsv)
echo "primary_expected	48297986"
test "$PRIM" = "48297986" || { echo "FAIL: $PRIM primary records, expected 48297986 (2 x 24,148,993 pairs)"; exit 1; }
echo "identity	primary records == 2 x read pairs"

# bowtie2 reports its own overall alignment rate; assert a floor only, since the exact value
# is a property of this library and reference rather than something fixed by construction.
RATE=$(awk '/overall alignment rate/{gsub("%","",$1); print $1}' /tmp/bt2align.log)
echo "overall_alignment_rate	$RATE"
awk -v r="$RATE" 'BEGIN{ if (r+0 < 90) { print "FAIL: alignment rate " r "% is below 90%"; exit 1 } }' || exit 1

printf 'clock_primary_mapped\t48198738\n'
printf 'clock_primary_mapq30\t40042364\n'
PM=$(awk -F'\t' '$1=="primary_mapped"{print $2}' /tmp/counts.tsv)
PQ=$(awk -F'\t' '$1=="primary_mapq30"{print $2}' /tmp/counts.tsv)
if [ "$PM" = "48198738" ] && [ "$PQ" = "40042364" ]; then
  printf 'invariance\tmapped and mapq30 match the clock exactly\n'
else
  printf 'invariance\tDIFFERS from clock: mapped=%s mapq30=%s -- a finding, not a failure\n' "$PM" "$PQ"
fi

{ echo -e "observable\tvalue"
  echo -e "bowtie2_wall_s\t$WALL"
  echo -e "overall_alignment_rate\t$RATE"
  cat /tmp/counts.tsv
} > /tmp/clock.tsv

uname -m | awk '{print "arch\t"$1}'
grep -m1 "CPU part" /proc/cpuinfo | awk '{print "cpu_part\t"$4}'
echo "BOWTIE2 CLOCK OK"
